qc.label_under_test: Weak, dense hum (11% of tokens reach 0.1 of a small max) that rises on talk-based mental-health treatment and the writing around it: counselling, therapy sessions, psychiatrists, psychoanalysis, psychodynamic work, support groups where people talk through their problems (about 0.2-0.65); mental-health book outlines and speech therapy also lift it (inverse found 0.46-0.55). Physical medicine (surgery, dentistry, nursing, vets) hums at the 0.1-0.2 baseline. Lateness: plain 'too late' / 'ran late' stays near zero, BUT the feeders' late signal does carry through in the discovered-too-late construction ('noticed / realised / found out too late that ...', 0.2-0.45 peaking on ' late'), so 'lateness adds nothing' was too strong.

neighbours.label: Weak, dense hum (11% of tokens reach 0.1 of a small max) that rises (about 0.3-0.55) on the vocabulary and settings of talking therapies: counsellor/counselling, therapist, psychiatrist, psychologist, psychoanalyst, psychodynamic/psychotherapy, group therapy, support groups, and also speech therapy (0.33-0.46). A crisis followed by 'weekly sessions' already lifts it before any profession is named. A plain paraphrase of talking about feelings with no care words stays near baseline (0.16), as do 'retail therapy', physical medicine (surgery, dentistry, nursing, vets) and cardiology (0.06-0.2). Lateness: lowercase 'found out / realised / discovered too late that ...' stays at baseline (0.08-0.17, not peaking on ' late'), so the earlier discovered-too-late clause did not replicate; only the capitalised headline 'Too Little too Late?' (0.35) carries a late signal. The spelling-piece feeders (ap/ag/pend/sp|ät) leave no lateness meaning here: German 'Verspätung' is near zero.
